Neutralization was increased when each Nb was fused as trimers using flexible GGGGS(x3) linkers and connected to human IgG1 Fc. Mutation E484K reduced or abolished neutralization by Nb17, Nb19 and Nb56, indicating this is an epitope residue. The Nbs also did not neutralize the triple mutation K417N, E484K, and N501Y. The Nb56 trimer was still able to neutralize mutant E484K and the triple mutant KEN.

The neutralization activity of the epitope-specific mAb (which had only six amino acid changes from its inferred germline precursor) and its germline predecessors against MERS-CoV S1-pseudotyped viruses in Huh-7 cells was evaluated. The mAb was neutralizing (IC50 = 0.003 ug ml<sup>-1</sup>).The reversion of the only mutation in the heavy chain (S59N) did not have any effect on neutralizing activity. Reversion of the three framework somatic mutations of the mAb to their germline counterparts markedly reduced the neutralization potency.

The critical epitope residues of SARS2-02 and SARS2-55 on the SARS-CoV-2 S were determined by analysis of neutralization escape mutants, isolated by passaging a VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2-S chimeric virus in the presence of neutralizing mAbs. Neutralization by mAbs SARS2-02 and SARS2-55 was abolished with G446D/V, L452R, and E484K substitutions. The epitope-specific mAbs blocked the binding of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein to ACE2.

The epitope-specific SARS2-02 and SARS2-55 mAbs neutralized authentic SARS-CoV-2 virus infection, using a focus-reduction neutralization test (FRNT) and Vero E6 cells, Vero-TMRPSS2, and Vero-TMPRSS2-ACE2 cells. SARS2-02 mAb retained neutralizing activity when added post-attachment, although the potency was reduced slightly (~2- to 4-fold, p < 0.05) relative to pre-attachment neutralization titers. MAb SARS2-02 neutralized SARS-CoV-2 virus infection of Vero-TMPRSS2-ACE2 cells, that ectopically express human ACE2 and TMPRSS2, but did not efficiently neutralized infection when added post-attachment, indicating the ability to neutralize at a post-attachment step depended on expression levels of viral entry factors and the cell line. MAb SARS2-02 showed reduced neutralization against recombinant chimeric WA1/2020 viruses encoding the spike protein from variants B.1.351 or B.1.1.28, with mutation E484K, or variant B.1.1.7 with E484K. SARS2-02 also showed reduced neutralization against variants B.1.429 (L452R), B.1.617.1, B.1.617.2 and B.1.526 (S477N or E484K).

The epitope-specific SARS2-02 mAb neutralized SARS-CoV-2 variant B.1.1.7 virus infection, using a focus-reduction neutralization test (FRNT). MAb SARS2-02 showed reduced neutralization against variant B.1.1.7 with mutation E484K.
